transcript:
IncidentsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated GPU OOM and container restarts on prod-serving-pool-3. 42 restarts in last 5m, spike aligns with large prefill requests with long-context inputs. Sample error: `CUDA out of memory` and `container killed by OOM`. Paging oncall.
Sam: I see the alerts, looking at tails now.
Maria: seeing repeated `CUDARuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` followed by `SIGKILL` for model-worker pods. Dumping sample logs to thread.
Maria: ```
2026-03-15T01:02:13Z model-worker-23 ERROR Runtime: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at /workspace/runner/infer.cpp:412
stack: 0x7f3b2...
killed by SIGKILL
```
Liam: nodes with the most restarts also reported `gpu0: ecc error` earlier and then kernel-level OOM, looks like memory fragmentation + large prefill allocations.
Nisha: customers hitting errors are mostly on high-context endpoints (long legal docs ingestion). CS reports 3 customers with >50 failed requests each in last 10m.
CustomerSuccess: Confirmed — Customer "AcmeLegal" saw repeated 500s. They're asking for ETA.
Sam: Immediate mitigation options: 1) add routing rule to divert requests with prefill size > 32k tokens to a smaller-ctx model variant; 2) enable prefill trimming policy to drop oldest context during prefill; 3) temporarily increase pool capacity (if spare GPUs available) or reduce concurrency on affected nodes.
Jen: @Sam can you try routing rule + concurrency throttle? I'll take handoff in 10min.
Sam: Applying quick router patch: setting `max_prefill_tokens=32768` on route `prod-longctx` and adding fallback to `m-small-ctx` at 10% traffic.
Sam: ```bash
# patch router configmap
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap router-config -p '{"data":{"max_prefill_tokens":"32768","fallback_route":"m-small-ctx:0.1"}}'
```
Maria: Also lowered node concurrency on pool-3 from 8 -> 4 to reduce concurrent prefill memory pressure. Patch applied.
Maria: ```bash
kubectl -n infra set env ds/model-worker MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 --selector=pool=prod-serving-pool-3
```
Liam: I see immediate drop in new OOMs on logs for patched nodes, but still seeing older pods flapping. Suggest cordon/drain the worst offenders and evict to fresh nodes to clear fragmentation.
Nisha: CS drafted a customer message: "We're experiencing intermittent 500s for large-context requests. We've applied routing and throttling mitigations and are actively monitoring. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary." Should we send now?
Jen: Send an initial note to affected customers now with ETA 30m; we'll follow with root cause once stabilized.
CustomerSuccess: Sending now.
PagerDuty: Pager duty note: oncall shift handoff in 10m from Sam -> Jen.
Sam: Handoff: traced root cause likely memory fragmentation from repeated very large prefill allocations causing CUDA allocator to fail even when nominal free memory exists. Repro steps attached. Current state: router limit + fallback applied, concurrency reduced, cordon scheduled for three noisy nodes and a rolling-restart of worker DaemonSet in progress.
Sam: repro snippet we used: ```python
# simulate long prefill
input_tokens = 70000
resp = client.generate(model='m-64k', prompt=long_doc)
# observe allocation spike and cuda OOM
```
Liam: Ops note: draining node n-prod-03 now. Using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to force reschedule.
Maria: Rolling restart completed for worker DS on pool-3. New pods stable so far, no OOMs in last 3m on fresh pods.
Jen: Taking over oncall. Summary for next oncall:
- Trigger: burst of very large prefill requests (>48k tokens) causing fragmentation and CUDA OOMs -> SIGKILL -> container restarts
- Mitigations applied: router `max_prefill_tokens=32768`, fallback to `m-small-ctx` at 10%, MAX_CONCURRENCY lowered to 4 for pool-3, cordoned/drained noisy nodes, rolling restart of model-worker DS
- Customer impact: ~3 customers with repeated 500s, overall error rate peaked at 6% for long-ctx endpoints; general endpoints unaffected. CS notified customers; initial message sent.
- Next steps: engineering task to implement allocator-level defrag and pre-alloc guard; add runbook step to auto-throttle prefill >32k; evaluate automatic routing to quantized variants under memory pressure.
Jen: I'll monitor for 30m then update with timeline for RCA. If error rate rises again I'll escalate to infra-sre.
Sam: Thanks all. Small ask — create an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime for RCA with priority P1.
Nisha: Ticket created: INC-2026-1223 assigned to eng-runtime.
IncidentsBot: Incident acknowledged and handoff complete. Continuing monitoring; closing pager but leaving incident thread open for RCA notes. :white_check_mark:
